newsitem.title: UK: Kazakhstan raises $200 mln in international market.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan raises $200 mln in international market.

text.p: Kazakhstan launched its first bond in the international markets on Monday, raising $200 million with a three-year issue.

Dutch bank ABN AMRO Hoare Govett organised the bond for the oil-rich central Asian republic, which was priced to yield 9.3 percent, or 3.5 percentage points above comparable U.S. Treasury notes. The spread was just inside the level at which Russia's recent $1.0 billion debut Eurobond issue was trading.
"We are delighted with the issue. It has got the broadest possible distribution," a dealer at ABN AMRO said.
Around 40 percent was sold in Europe, 40 percent in the U.S., and the remaining 20 percent was placed in Asia, ABN said.
The bond issue followed a series of economic presentations around the world by Kazakh officials and investment bankers from ABN AMRO.

Grigory Marchenko, chairman of Kazakhstan's National Security Committee, told investors at a meeting in New York last week that the country did not need money at present but was seeking to establish itself internationally. "We do it for the sake of putting our name on the map," Marchenko said.

Prime Minister Akezhan Kazhegeldin said his country stacked up favourably against other similarly rated countries in terms of external debt and natural resources but admitted there were concerns about projects to transport Kazakh oil and gas to the world market.
